entities.summary: Dennis Carl Wilson was an American musician, singer, and songwriter who co-founded the Beach Boys in 1961. He served as the band's drummer and was the middle brother of bandmates Brian and Carl Wilson. The only dedicated surfer in the group, his lifestyle embodied the “California myth” that inspired and was celebrated in many of the band's early songs. Over time, Wilson also emerged as a songwriter and contributed original material to the band's repertoire, including "Forever" (1970), his best-known composition.
